courses.title: Academic Literacy and Ethos
courses.description: This course examines the role of post-secondary reading theory and concepts within literary works and other domains of the humanities. This examination is founded on an intensive study of post-secondary reading as a recursive and intellectual development of comprehension, analysis, problem-solving, reflective judgment, and interpretation skills through a range of challenging texts in multiple literary genres, as well as primary-source material from various cultural perspectives across the disciplines. Rhetorical comprehension promotes the development of a literary consciousness leading to personal and academic growth that will engage students as full participants in college, civic life, and global society.
courses.prerequisites: ESL D272. and ESL D273., or ESL D472. and ESL D473., or a qualifying score on the English as a Second Language Placement Test
courses.advisories: ENGL C1000 or ENGL C1000H or ESL D005.

courses.title: Reading Across the Disciplines
courses.description: This course is intended to improve comprehension of reading materials in a specific content-area course through the application of post-secondary reading strategies and critical analysis of reading materials. This course includes engagement in the development of reading comprehension using a diverse selection of literary genres from various cultural perspectives across the disciplines. It is an in-depth study of the reading discipline to promote analysis, problem-solving, reflective judgment, and interpretation skills, all of which foster intellectual growth.

metadata.Course Philosophy: It is essential to guide and support student in their efforts to critically understand collegiate course readings. The teaching of post-secondary reading moves beyond tutorial assistance and engages in an array of specific strategies and skills that students employ to improve and evolve comprehension and analysis of academic texts. Readers are introduced to the practice of metacognition and self-reflection concepts to build and strengthen rhetorical skills and abilities.
